Commentary.Commentary: The final session is set to begin. The Sri Lankan players stride out to the middle. They are followed by Kraigg Brathwaite and Jermaine Blackwood who walk out to open for West Indies. Lasith Embuldeniya to start with the new ball.
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

Right then. West Indies have a stiff mountain to climb, as they come out to chase a target of 348 runs. Let us also keep in mind, the purchase off the deck for the spinners. With the bowling line-up that Sri Lanka possess they can run riots with the ball.  But did you forget the miracle that the Windies pulled out in Antigua? During the first Test match against the Islanders. They battled throughout the last day to squeeze out a result. Can they repeat their heroics yet again, but this time away from home and alongwith a tricky condition? We shall find out soon, as the final session is not far away.

West Indies got a good start, courtesy of Rahkeem Cornwall. Soon, Jomel Warrican snared a wicket as well. It is what they desired, pick early wickets and not let Sri Lanka score freely. Although the team excelled in the first objective, they rather lost their track achieving their second goal. The third wicket stand proved to be costly for the visitors. The West Indies players were chirpy on the field but all gone quiet once the pair stitched a 100-run stand. That’s when they started losing the edge. It was deep in the second session, when Cornwall struck again to get rid of Dimuth Karunaratne. Also, Jomel Warrican sent back a new batter in Dhananjaya de Silva. Later, Mathews and Chandimal hit a few lusty blows before the hosts decided to declare.

Early Tea has been called here on Day 4! SRI LANKA have finally declared, looks like Dimuth Karunaratne was waiting for a biggie, but on a serious note, the hosts certainly hold the upper hand in this game. It was their experienced pair of Dimuth Karunaratne and Angelo Mathews who made sure to swell the lead consistently. The former slipped out of his chance of scoring a ton in each innings. Although, Mathews scored a composed innings and smacked 69 runs not out. Mathews kept going till the end and had his foot on the gas in the end. They have set up a target of 348 runs.

The second session is set to begin. The West Indies players stride out to the middle. Followed by Angelo Mathews and Dimuth Karunaratne who walk out to bat for the hosts. Jason Holder to start with the ball.
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Rahkeem Cornwall bowled throughout the first session as he was turning the ball sharply and making things happen. He took one wicket but would have another one if they had taken that LBW review against Dimuth Karunaratne. From the other end, Jomel Warrican was used mostly as he too was rolling his fingers nicely. Too early to call for the result but West Indies will be pretty pleased with a draw and if they aspire for something bigger, wickets are a must and that too at a rapid pace. We have an interesting session coming up. Do join us in a while.

A session which was started late due to rain, the hosts still hold an upper hand going into the break as they now lead by 240 runs. Dimuth Karunaratne and Angelo Mathews have done well to pass this session but they would look to score with more pace if they want to win this match, keeping the conditions in mind. Pathum Nissanka and Oshada Fernando fell cheaply but since then, these two have done well to build a partnership.

FOUR BYES! Full, around leg and spinning away. Oshada Fernando shoulders arms to it and the ball beats the leg slip as well. Boundary.
On middle, tucked to mid on.
Oshada Fernando walks out at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! West Indies need quick wickets and Cornwell gives them the start. A tossed up ball, full and down the leg side, spinning away as well. Pathum Nissanka gets low and looks to sweep but only manages some gloves on it towards the leg slip. Shai Hope there, dives to his right and takes a brilliant catch. An appeal and up goes the finger. Pathum Nissanka is not convinced that he got some bat on it but the UltraEdge shows a spike as it passes his glove.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Rahkeem Cornwall

Commentary.Commentary: Review! Pathum Nissanka decides to take a review for caught behind. The on-field decision is OUT. The UltraEdge shows clear spike and Pathum Nissanka has to depart. The original decision stands.
A full ball, on middle. Pathum Nissanka looks to sweep but gets a top edge. The ball lobs and falls in front of him. The keeper was trying to rush across but fails to reach on time.

Just short of the short extra cover fielder! A full ball, outside off. Dimuth Karunaratne goes inside-out and hits just over the short extra cover fielder. There is a run out chance as well but both the batters make their ground in time. A single.
Now serves a fuller length ball, on middle. Pathum Nissanka jams it out to mid on.
A length ball, outside off. Pathum Nissanka hops and punches it through cover-point for a couple of runs.
On a length, on middle, tucked to mid on.
Length again, on off. Pathum Nissanka defends it more off the other half towards backward point.
On a length, outside off. Nissanka taps it to gully.
Holder starts with a length ball, around off. Pathum Nissanka watchfully blocks it on the ground.
Who will bowl from the other end? Jason Holder it is. It won't be spin from both ends.
Flatter and outside off. Dimuth Karunaratne punches it to back to the bowler off the back foot. Just a single off the first over.
Short and outside off. Dimuth Karunaratne mistimes his slap to mid off.
Just short of the gully fielder. A full ball, on off. Dimuth Karunaratne prods and looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge to gully.
Tossed up, full and on middle. Pathum Nissanka gets on his knee and sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.
Short again, on middle. Pathum Nissanka defends it towards square leg.
Starts with a short ball, spilled down the leg side. Pathum Nissanka rocks back and leaves it alone.
